articles.headline: Inside Week 9 of CIAC football: A record-breaker, eight remain perfect and who's No. 1 now?
keyFacts: Ludlowe claimed the No. 1 spot in the GametimeCT Top 10 poll for the first time in program history following back-to-back wins over New Canaan.
Holy Cross senior Dae'Sean Graves broke the state career record for receptions with 227 during a 38-14 win over Woodland.
Eight undefeated high school football teams remain after Week 9 of the 2026 CIAC season.
body: St. Joseph's Justin Daniels (5) is chased across the backfield by New Canaan's Liam Danaher (56) during the CIAC football game between No. 2 St. Joseph and No. 3 New Canaan high schools. Friday November 6, 2026, New Canaan High School, New Canaan, Conn. (H John Voorhees III/Hearst Connecticut Media)
You can almost smell the turkey cooking.
Hard to believe, but we're already through Week 9 of the 2026 CIAC football season, and the annual Thanksgiving rivalry games are only three weeks away.
The second half of the campaign has really picked up the pace in terms of drama and key matchups.
One question still remains: Who's No. 1?
Coaches and even some players will say the rankings in the GametimeCT Top 10 poll don't matter. After all, rankings don't win championships.
Others are more outspoken and are definitely paying attention.
It's great for discussion, and the past two weeks have especially brought that to light.
New Canaan had held the No. 1 spot since the final poll of the 2024 season but has now lost two straight - to Ludlowe 34-31 and St. Joseph 21-14 .
That has knocked the Rams (6-2) down a couple of rungs, although they remain in the top half of the poll, currently at No. 3.

Last week, three teams split the 21 first-place votes. Ludlowe (8-0) took 11 and was propelled all the way from No. 6 to No. 1, the first time in the program's history it has been on top of the GametimeCT poll.
St. Joseph (7-0) took nine first-place votes and held in the No. 2 spot, and No. 6 Southington (7-1) earned one first-place vote.

And although it didn't receive a first-place vote, a case could be made for No. 5 Hand (8-0), which has the state's longest win streak at 16 and just knocked off Lyman Hall 35-14 in a battle of unbeatens .
Now, St. Joseph has its own win over New Canaan after holding off a comeback bid by the Rams for a 21-14 decision on Friday.
Is that enough to push the Hogs past the Falcons?
"Oh, we're No. 1 by far," said St. Joseph's Wisconsin-bound lineman Will Zaccagnino , clearly not mincing any words.
A week earlier, Ludlowe lineman Carlo Noecker gave his thoughts on who is the best.

"It's a little hard to believe 10 years ago this team couldn't get a single win," Noecker said. "Now we just knocked off the best powerhouse (New Canaan) in New England. It's unbelievable, but we know we're No. 1."
Time will tell, of course, and the next GametimeCT Top 10 comes out Monday.
Stay tuned.
Dae'Sean to remember
Two down, one to go.
Holy Cross senior Dae'Sean Graves broke a second state receiving record and moved closer to a third during the Crusaders' 38-14 win over Woodland on Friday.
Graves, a UConn commit, had six catches in the game and now has 227 in his career, breaking the old state mark of 226, set just last year by East Catholic's Joey Montalvo.
Montalvo, by the way, is a freshman on the Central Connecticut State football team.

The guy who has been throwing those passes to Graves for the past two seasons, quarterback Brady Lombardo, also hit two milestones on Friday, surpassing 2,000 passing yards for the season and 5,000 for his career.
The Lombardo-to-Graves combo has helped Holy Cross (7-1) win seven straight since an opening-week loss to Naugatuck.

Graves added to his state record with a touchdown reception, giving him 53 career touchdown receptions. He set that mark during a 52-13 win over Crosby on Oct. 23, surpassing the old high-water mark of 50, which had been held by Southington's Alex Jamele.
That's two, and Graves has a little more work to do for the trifecta. With 94 yards on Friday, he now has 3,434 career receiving yards, 437 short of Montalvo's 3,871.

He'll have a shot at it. The Crusaders have two more regular-season games remaining, against GNH on Nov. 12 and Wolcott on Thanksgiving, and are in good shape for a Class MM playoff berth, currently ranking second in the standings.
And then there were eight
Every year following Week 9 of the football season, GametimeCT puts together a breakdown of the remaining undefeated teams and looks at their chances of going 10-0 in the regular season.
It's pretty amazing how little consistency there is in the group from year to year.

In the four seasons since 2023, 33 teams have made it through Week 9 with perfect records. Only four teams have done it twice. That group includes Killingly and Windsor in both 2024 and 2025, Naugatuck in 2023 and 2026, and Hand in 2024 and 2026.
It shows just how tough it is to win football games.
There were nine teams unbeaten following Week 9 last fall , and this season, there are eight, after Southington fell to New Britain 28-27 on Thursday, and Lyman Hall lost to Hand 35-14 on Friday.
The undefeated teams left are Hand, Ludlowe, Masuk, Naugatuck, New London, North Branford and Plainville, all 8-0, and St. Joseph, which is 7-0.
All eight have at least one difficult test remaining, so 10-0 is by no means a lock for anyone.
Giddy up.
Bullet points

New Britain scored a 28-27 win over previously unbeaten Southington (7-1), with the difference being a blocked PAT by Javier Zenquis, a scout player. The Golden Hurricanes are 6-2, with their only losses coming against defending state champs Greenwich and New Canaan.
Hand senior running back Lucca Boyce surpassed 3,000 career rushing yards during the Tigers' 35-14 win over Lyman Hall (7-1) . No. 5 Hand (8-0) owns the state's longest win streak at 16.
Guilford (7-1) overcame Branford (5-3) in a low-scoring affair 7-6 , with Shane Connelly scoring the Grizzlies' lone touchdown on an 81-yard pass from Ryan Lynch.
No. 1 Ludlowe followed up its huge win at New Canaan with a 40-13 win over Trumbull .
Naugatuck (8-0) got two rushing touchdowns and a touchdown pass from Qwentarvus Lee and won 41-12 over Seymour (5-3).
Maloney (6-2) gave itself a massive boost in the Class L playoff hunt with a 55-40 win over Windsor (4-4). The Spartans have been averaging more than 40 points per game.
Simsbury (7-1) defeated Newington 27-7 for its seventh win of the season. The Trojans had just four wins combined in the last three seasons.
Cheshire (6-2) won its third straight game 35-10 over Sheehan (4-4) and is now in third place in the Class M standings.
Darien (5-3) jumped into the top eight in Class L with a 34-14 win over Ridgefield (4-4). The Blue Wave will finish the regular season against Stamford and New Canaan.
Up next
Time has flown by.
We are getting down to crunch time, as we amazingly get ready to enter Week 10 of the football season.

There are a bushel of key games on deck, including a pair of matchups of ranked teams, when No. 1 Ludlowe faces No. 8 Staples in Westport on Friday at 7 p.m., and No. 2 St. Joseph hosts No. 4 Greenwich on Saturday at noon.
The SCC is loaded with big games, including Lyman Hall looking to rebound from its first loss of the season by hosting Law on Friday at 6:30 p.m.

articles.headline: Manchester City player ratings vs Nottingham Forest: Rayan Cherki sparks brief hope but defensive disasters cost Enzo Maresca dear
keyFacts: Manchester City suffered a third consecutive Premier League defeat, losing 3-1 away to Nottingham Forest.
Liam Delap scored twice for Nottingham Forest against his former club, securing the home victory.
Rayan Cherki scored a half-volley for Manchester City, but the team remains six points behind league leaders Arsenal.
body: FBL-EUR-C1-LEIPZIG-MAN CITY - AFP Liam Delap scored twice against the club where he came through the academy as Manchester City slipped to a third straight Premier League defeat, beaten 3-1 by a Nottingham Forest side that had not scored at home all season.

Maresca recalled Josko Gvardiol, Ruben Dias and Jeremy Doku, but City were behind inside six minutes when Gvardiol was bundled off the ball by Jair Cunha, who strode forward to roll a low finish into the bottom corner. On 18 minutes Xaver Schlager beat Elliot Anderson to a 50/50 in midfield and Delap ran from halfway to rifle past Gianluigi Donnarumma. It was the earliest City had been 2-0 down in a Premier League game since November 2019.

Cherki's stunning half-volley on 52 minutes sparked a long spell of City pressure, and the visitors finished with 78% of the ball and 33 touches in the Forest box to 14. But Delap finished off a counter on 73 minutes, lashing Morgan Gibbs-White's pass into the top corner. City, who won their first seven league games, stay second on 21 points but are now six behind leaders Arsenal, while Forest climb out of the bottom three to 16th.
Below, GOAL rates Manchester City's players from the City Ground...
Goalkeeper & Defence
Gianluigi Donnarumma (5/10): Made two saves and had no chance with any of the goals, but flapped at a whipped James McAtee corner in the first half and was fortunate nobody in red got a touch.

Abdukodir Khusanov (6/10): Started at right-back and was rarely the problem as the defence unravelled around him. Played the full 90 minutes and did not escape every test, conceding a corner from a dangerous Daniel Munoz cross in the first half.

Ruben Dias (6/10): Wore the armband on his return to the side, but gave away the free-kick from which Cunha shanked a first-half chance wide. City's back line was nowhere to be seen as Delap ran from halfway for Forest's second.

Marc Guehi (6/10): Whipped in a wonderful cross from the left that Enzo Fernandez should have converted on 25 minutes, and also picked out Erling Haaland for City's first effort on target. Replaced by Matheus Nunes at half-time.

Josko Gvardiol (4/10): A night to forget at left-back. Took a heavy touch and was bundled off the ball far too easily by Cunha for the sixth-minute opener. He was replaced by Nico O'Reilly at the break.
Midfield

Elliot Anderson (6/10): A tough return to his old club. Lost the 50/50 with Schlager that sent Delap away for Forest's second, but grew into the game after that, threading the pass that started the move in which Haaland was denied on the line and volleying straight at Matz Sels.

Enzo Fernandez (5/10): Should have halved the deficit on 25 minutes but headed over from close range from Guehi's cross. Was later robbed by Murillo in a move that nearly brought Forest a third, and was booed off when replaced by Phil Foden on 78 minutes.

Rayan Cherki (8/10): City's standout performer. Played Iliman Ndiaye in for City's first chance, then pulled one back on 52 minutes, meeting Doku's deflected cross with a sweet left-footed half-volley into the top corner for his fifth Premier League goal of the season.
Attack

Iliman Ndiaye (7/10): City's liveliest outlet on the right. Picked out Doku for an early shot, combined well with Nunes after the break, and his burst forward forced Dan Ndoye into a cynical foul and a yellow card.

Jeremy Doku (6/10): Had an early shot blocked and his final ball was often lacking, but he came alive after the break. Got in behind Munoz to deliver the cross that deflected off Ryan Yates for Cherki's goal, and gave the wing-back such a hard time that he was withdrawn on 65 minutes.

Erling Haaland (6/10): Rounded Sels on 41 minutes only to be denied on the line by Cunha, and scooped over from a Nunes cross after the break. Rarely got the service he needed against a deep Forest defence.
Substitutes & Manager
Matheus Nunes (7/10): Replaced Guehi at the break and gave City more thrust down the right, delivering the cross that Haaland scooped over. Also blocked a Delap shot and stopped Gibbs-White late on.

Nico O'Reilly (6/10): Replaced Gvardiol at half-time and pushed on from left-back. Doku slipped him in behind for a low delivery that Murillo cleared, though he could not make proper contact with a Nunes cross just after the restart.
Phil Foden (6/10): Replaced Fernandez on 78 minutes and tried to make things happen, drawing a late booking for Luca Netz, but Forest saw the game out.

Enzo Maresca (4/10): His three changes backfired, with the recalled Gvardiol at fault for the opener. His side improved after the break, but City have now lost three in a row in the league after winning their first seven.

articles.headline: Commanders stance on potential Brandon Aiyuk addition revealed by NFL insiders
keyFacts: NFL insiders Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport reported that the Washington Commanders are not ruling out adding wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk this season.
Aiyuk is filing for reinstatement to the NFL and previously expressed interest in joining Washington to reunite with quarterback Jayden Daniels.
Potential complications like money owed to the San Francisco 49ers and uncertain health mean an immediate deal is not guaranteed.
body: The Washington Commanders aren't out of the NFC East race just yet, so seeing the team make an impactful mid-season addition isn't out of the question.

After losing Terry McLaurin to season-ending IR, it would not be a total surprise if the Commanders showed interest in upgrading the wide receiver room. One name has recently popped back up as an option for the Commanders: Brandon Aiyuk.

He's filing for reinstatement to the NFL finally, and could be available soon. So, what are the Commanders' thoughts on adding Aiyuk? ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport revealed the Commanders aren't ruling out adding Aiyuk yet this season.
Commanders aren't ruling out adding Brandon Aiyuk just yet

"The Commanders haven't completely abandoned the idea of adding wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk, who was rumored during the summer to end up in Washington, according to sources," Schefter and Rapoport report.
This is a very interesting update for the Commanders, as their interest in Aiyuk is seemingly real enough that he has a chance to join Washington this season.
During the offseason, Aiyuk made it very clear he wanted to join the Commanders and reunite with Jayden Daniels. That didn't happen, as he needed to file for reinstatement.
As the NFL enters Week 9, Aiyuk has finally taken the first step toward an NFL return. With the San Francisco 49ers all but guaranteed to move on from him, Aiyuk could wind up with the Commanders.
But, will he actually come to Washington? It's not a guarantee, especially since there are some significant complications with Aiyuk's return to the NFL.
He reportedly owes the 49ers $13 million, which is obviously a big problem. Besides, he might not be fully healthy or in shape to play in the league right away.
While he's making a push to return to the league, he hasn't been reinstated, and it might take some time before he is able to join an NFL team again.

So, while the Commanders aren't ruling out adding Aiyuk, such an addition is far from a guarantee this season. This might be something that happens over the offseason, rather than at some point during the 2026 season.

articles.headline: What we know so far after Polish gunman opens fire in Krakow main square
keyFacts: Six people were killed and sixteen injured after a gunman opened fire in Krakow's main square before being arrested, officials said.
A minister said early investigations indicate the arrested 25-year-old Polish suspect was inspired by far-right ideologies.
Krakow's mayor declared a mourning period until November 11, while Prime Minister Donald Tusk is scheduled to give an address.
body: - Published

At least six people have been killed and several others injured after a gunman suspected to have ties to the far-right opened fire in central Krakow, the second largest city in Poland. Here's everything we know so far.
How did the attack unfold?
The attack began shortly before 15:00 local time (14:00 GMT) in Krakow's Main Market Square, the bustling central point of the city.
Police said a man drove into the square before beginning to fire "at random people from his car".
Footage from the scene shows scenes of panic as people fled, with the sound of gunfire clearly heard.
A passing tram was shot at during the apparently random attack, shattering windows but no passengers were injured.
Armed officers raced to the scene and engaged in a gunfight with the attacker, who was shot within three minutes of the attack beginning, preventing a further massacre, officials said.
The gunman was shot but is alive and has been arrested.
Distressing footage authenticated by BBC Verify shows the moment a police officer confronts the suspect on the ground before firing his weapon several times.
The officer then falls to the ground, apparently having been injured himself.
Shop windows in the square have signs of damage, seemingly from bullets, with glass shards scattered along the floor.
City officials have urged people who live in the city and tourists to stay away from the area while an investigation continues.
How many people have died and been injured?
Six people - four women and two men - are confirmed to have been killed, including a foreign national.
Sixteen people, including five foreigners and the attacker, were taken to hospital. Among those being treated are two police officers who were shot while detaining the attacker.

One of the police officers was described as being in a "very critical condition" by a Polish government minister after being shot three times while arresting the attacker. The officer is undergoing surgery, he added.
Polish authorities have not confirmed the names and ages of the other victims.
What do we know about the suspect and motive?
Police have identified the attacker as a 25-year-old Polish man but have not confirmed his name.
The suspect was wearing "military-style attire" and had a military-grade weapon, according to a police spokesperson. However, authorities have confirmed the attacker was not a soldier.
"Many pieces of weapons and ammunition were found in his vehicle", the spokesperson added.
Polish media has reported the suspect had a firearms permit and may have obtained the weapons from his family home.
A minister has said early investigations indicate he was inspired by "far-right ideologies". The minister also described him as an "ultra-nationalist" without giving further details.
His home is being searched with support from counter-terrorism police.
How did witnesses describe the attack?
The shooting happened in one of the largest medieval squares in Europe, a busy location which is also a popular tourist destination.
Jonathan Balshaw from Ipswich was there with his Polish girlfriend Dominika. The couple were outside St Mary's Basilica, in the corner of the square, when the shooting started.
Jonathan said: "We ran down the side of the church and through the side door and hid with several other people until the gunfire died down.
"A lot of shots were fired, more than 20 with it sounding like multiple different firearms - there were two distinctly different noises."
Caitlin Shasby from Newcastle arrived in Krakow yesterday with her friend Jon for a long weekend.
She said they heard shots from their hotel room but were not sure what was happening until their hotel rang them and told them to "stay in our rooms until further notice".
What has the reaction been in Poland and internationally?
Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk is on his way to Krakow and is expected to give an address later on Saturday.
Earlier, he said he was being kept informed by the interior minister and that police were investigating "the background and all the circumstances".
Krakow Mayor Åukasz GibaÅa has signed an order declaring a period of mourning in the city which will last until Wednesday, November 11.
President Karol Nawrocki said he was "deeply concerned" and was awaiting "a full explanation of the circumstances surrounding these tragic events".
US ambassador to Poland Tom Rose described it as a "savage and murderous attack".
The EU's top diplomat, Kaja Kallas, said the shooting was "a tragedy that will be felt far beyond Poland".

articles.headline: Star Wars Zero Company studio Bit Reactor lays off staff, a month after bringing furloughed developers back
keyFacts: Developer Bit Reactor has laid off an unspecified number of staff members.
The layoffs occurred one month after the studio brought some previously furloughed developers back to work following the launch of Star Wars Zero Company.
Bit Reactor has not disclosed the total number of employees affected by these recent job cuts.
body: Star Wars Zero Company developer Bit Reactor has laid off an unspecified number of staff, a month after bringing some of its furloughed team back to work.
Several developers announced on LinkedIn on Friday, 6th November, that they had been let go, as first reported by Bespin Bulletin. Bit Reactor hasn't said how many people are affected.

Among them is senior environment artist Ryan Lopez, who spent three and a half years working on Zero Company, from pre-production to launch, and was laid off after a three-month furlough. UI engineer Tyler Eichten, who worked on much of the on-screen UI for the game's tactical missions, and Ryan Mosher from the QA team have also confirmed they were let go.
"While it stings, I'm really proud of what we built together," Lopez wrote. "It was a privilege to ship a game with you."

Bit Reactor furloughed most of its staff in the weeks before Zero Company launched on 27th August, with one source putting the figure at roughly 80 percent. The studio appeared to have run out of money just short of release.

The game did well regardless, and is thought to have sold more than a million copies within a month. Then, in a message shared on Bluesky on 7th October, CEO Greg Foertsch said the studio had "started the process of returning more of our team back to work". Asking staff to step away so close to launch was "an incredibly difficult decision", he said, "but one that was necessary to help us eventually bring as many people back as possible".
It's thought more than half the studio returned, though not everyone went back on full pay. It's not clear whether any of those who returned were among the people laid off this week.

In Eurogamer's Star Wars Zero Company review, we awarded the game four out of five stars, saying, "an already winning genre is matched with the perfect setting in this earnest, heartfelt, smart and slightly ramshackle turn-based tactics gem".

articles.headline: How to connect an Apple Pencil to your iPad
keyFacts: Linking an Apple Pencil to an iPad requires following a specific pairing process that depends on the model of the stylus.
Compatibility issues can occur because different Apple Pencil versions only work with specific iPad models according to Apple.
Troubleshooting steps for pairing problems include physically reconnecting the stylus, restarting the iPad, updating software, and checking Bluetooth settings.
body: How to connect an Apple Pencil to your iPad
Getting your Apple Pencil linked with your iPad is easy, as long as they're compatible.
We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

Contrary to the impression Apple gives, you don't need an Apple Pencil to use an iPad. As input accessories go, you're probably better off picking up a keyboard and mouse for your iPad first. But with a giant touchscreen, illustration and handwritten notes are obvious selling points, and you need some sort of stylus to make that work. The company is naturally going to upsell you on its own accessories, regardless of whether cheaper alternatives might get the job done.

Pairing an Apple Pencil to an iPad is dead simple, for the most part. But there is a process, plus surprising compatibility issues can crop up. You'd think a stylus would be one of the simplest accessories possible, but Apple's evolving iPad ambitions have created a few roadblocks.
We'll also deal with a few general troubleshooting issues, though chances are that you'll be up and drawing within a few minutes.
How to pair any Apple Pencil to an iPad

The exact pairing process depends on the Pencil model you own. In the case of the USB-C Apple Pencil, slide open the end of the stylus to reveal the USB-C port, then connect it to your iPad using an appropriate cable. A pairing prompt should appear on-screen, at which point all you need to do is hit Tap to Connect. As a bonus, your Pencil will charge at the same time. This also works with the iPhone Duo, which is only compatible with the USB-C Pencil.

The process is even simpler with the Apple Pencil Pro. Once you've unboxed it, let it clip magnetically to the long side of your iPad. That's it — you're ready to go in seconds. This is also how you charge the Pencil Pro, and how you'll likely store it most of the time unless you're worried about it being knocked off inside a bag or suitcase. Meanwhile, the second-generation Pencil pairs just like the Pro.

If you've got a first-gen stylus, you'll need to remove its cap, plug it in via its Lightning connector, then tap Pair. In case you're using the original Pencil with a USB-C base iPad (either the 10th gen or A16 model), you'll need a Lightning to USB-C adapter.
Unfortunately, the first-gen model and USB-C Pencil must be re-paired every time you restart your iPad or disable Bluetooth.
Fixing Apple Pencil pairing issues

Your first concern is those compatibility issues we mentioned. The first-gen Pencil is intended for Lightning-equipped iPads; it won't work with newer USB-C iPad mini, Air or Pro models. The base iPad models from 2022 and 2025 support it with an adapter. Meanwhile, the second-gen Pencil is limited to certain iPad models that aren't too old or new.

The USB-C Pencil is more broadly supported, while the Pencil Pro only works with a narrow slice of iPad Air, Mini and Pro models. It's smart to check Apple's Apple Pencil compatibility list to confirm, especially if you're planning to buy a new iPad or Pencil.

If your Pencil pairs but is still having trouble, physically reconnect it to your iPad. Once that's done, restart your iPad by holding down a volume button and the power button, then swiping the power-off slider when it appears. Hold the power button again after a moment to turn it back on. (On an older iPad with a Home button, just hold the power button.) Update your iPad at Settings > General > Software Update too.

Try re-pairing your Pencil, which may involve physically disconnecting the stylus from your iPad first. If nothing's working, navigate to Settings > Bluetooth and double-check that Bluetooth is enabled. If your Pencil already shows as Connected, tap the i icon next to it, then Forget this Device. Retry the appropriate pairing process.

In some circumstances, it may be that your Pencil doesn't have enough power to pair, so simply leaving it plugged in for a while could do the trick. Apple also suggests removing any cases or covers from your iPad on the off chance they're interfering. But if you've reached that level of desperation, you'll probably need to book a service appointment at your local Apple retailer, hopefully covered by AppleCare.

articles.headline: Retail World of Warcraft is one lonely treadmill; fortunately, Classic and Forever remind us that it doesn’t have to be.
keyFacts: The author stated that modern Retail World of Warcraft has evolved into a fast-paced, season-based game that feels like a lonely chore rather than a true MMO.

The author noted that World of Warcraft Classic and Forever succeed by requiring a massive time commitment, which fosters genuine social connections, meaningful gear attachment, and a thriving community.
The author suggested that Blizzard should evaluate future additions by questioning whether they reduce time commitments or increase accessibility, in order to preserve the game's core strengths.
body: Ok, I'll come out and say it. Modern World of Warcraft, or Midnight, in all of its convoluted story-driven glory, with its systems on systems, its currencies on currencies, and high-octane pacing, isn't an MMO. It's just not. At least not to me.

Every gamer has a backlog — and that’s no different for us at TechRadar Gaming. From the Backlog is a series about overdue first plays, revisiting classics, returning to online experiences, or rediscovering and appreciating established favorites in new ways. Read the full series here.

I know that's a big ol' bold statement, and I get it; you're probably sat there thinking: "Zak, what the hell are you on about? Stop being an overly dramatic journalist trying to clickbait us all into reading your long-winded waffling diatribe". But hear me out before you reach for the Dirge.

If you boiled down the current iteration of the game in a pot, and stripped away the marketing hype, and the hyper-attentive gameplay, Midnight, retail, it's not actually that different from something like Call of Duty, or Overwatch. Not at its heart. It's seasonal; it's mostly queue-based, with as much commitment as I have to that chilli I cooked up three months back that's still sitting in my freezer.
Where it all began
I've been playing World of Warcraft since 2006. Over 20 years, stuck with the same video game, handing Blizzard my hard-earned cash for a monthly sub.

I've done it all. I was a Priest Class Leader at the age of 14, raiding in Molten Core, BWL and AQ40 (mad respect to Fracture Bloodfeather EU). I then main tanked through The Burning Crusade and Wrath of the Lich King expansions on a Dwarf Warrior. After that, a Guild Leader and Raid Leader in Cataclysm and Mists of Pandaria, healing on my Priest. Finally, ending as a Retribution Paladin in Warlords of Draenor and beyond.

The game got me into UI development; it got me into PC building. I studied how to create textures and TGA files in Photoshop, built rudimentary addons with Lua, and created a reasonably successful UI series. It taught me about design, about triage, about optimization. I owe my career to this game in many ways.

But during the Legion expansion, going into Battle for Azeroth, something flipped. I'd gotten used to the pace, the tempo. I tolerated the timed high-end Mythic+ 5-man dungeons, the constant weekly epic treadmill, and how impatient the community had become.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.

And of course I managed to continually decode the never-ending slew of multiplying vertical progression systems and catch-up mechanics with ever more convoluted naming schemes, to stay at the top of my game.

But it wasn't long before I came to the realisation that I had no close community anymore. I wasn't making new acquaintances or friends in the same way I had through previous expansions; I didn't feel tied to any one guild, or server, or faction, or anything. And slowly, my love for the game faded.

The sub was paused on and off sporadically. I'd jump back in every expansion launch, trying to get into it, trying to convince myself that this was the one, but it was a constant struggle to stay committed, to enjoy it. In a world that felt so empty, so devoid of life. It turned into a lonely chore, rather than a fun pastime to rid myself of the day's stress, and I couldn't pinpoint why I was getting so burnt out by it. At least not until very recently.
The key concept: Time

The last few months I've been playing World of Warcraft: Classic, (of course on the run-up to the WoW Forever launch), and that, that has provided me with clarity on what it was I didn't understand was missing from Retail.

Vanilla Classic, even today, is still ridiculously popular. More so than Mists of Pandaria, or any other version of the rebooted game. It's odd, right? It launched in 2019, and yet the servers are still bristling with people running 40-man raids, doing PvP, and are home to thriving economies, guilds, events, and more. You can barely move in Stormwind on some servers. And that's despite the game being well and truly "worked out" years ago. But why?

Simply put, it's time. The game in its modern state, maybe accidentally, maybe on purpose, gave up what made it so special. What made it an MMO to begin with. All in an attempt to try and attract more people to the player base, and bring more subs in. And it did so by, conversely, becoming more accessible.

Because everything is so fast, and there's a constant treadmill with extensive catch-up mechanics, there's no commitment. You lose attachment to what it is you're doing, and as a result, nothing matters. On average, to go from level 1 to the max cap of 90 in Midnight, it can take anywhere between 12 and 18 hours. For an established player, it can be less than eight.

As a result, people hop about constantly. Is your class not performing well? Is another now at the top of the Mythic+ logs? Just create a new character, and in less than half a day you can be gearing up for high-end Mythic raiding.

Even worse still, if you're low on cash, you can get some from Blizzard's in-game store with three mouse clicks and a healthy chunk of your own cash. That will allow you to buy a slew of gear from the latest content directly on the game's player Auction House.

The modern games' profession systems are also a mess, and it takes a degree in data analytics to understand half of it at a glance. Hell, you can even skip the bulk of the levelling entirely if you want and just pay for a character boost if need be, no matter what state your account is in.

If you do decide to skip the boost, then even the levelling journey itself feels disconnected from the community. Most just spam dungeons and get pooled up with players from all over the continent, never to see them again, running them as fast as possible with mass AOE pulls.

Or if that's not to your taste, you pick a specific past expansion from the game's lengthy list to level through instead. In this case, you'll see no max-level players at all, only the select few that have chosen to also level in that specific piece of content.
This is all as you barrel through levels a mile a minute, learning new skills faster than you can acclimatise, and watch as your gear becomes redundant in less than 15 minutes.
What WoW: Forever & Classic get right

And this is what Classic and Forever get right. It takes an age to level; it really does. I have a 32 Hunter currently, a 21 Warrior, and a 21 Priest on Classic. I'm halfway to 60 (in number only) on that Hunter. It's one of the fastest classes to level in Vanilla WoW, and my playtime is 2 days and 1 hour to get that far. I could've levelled five classes in Retail in that time. And still, I've got another 4 to 6 days to get to max level, if I don't mill about.

And here's the thing: because it takes so long, I've done an incredible amount of extra content outside of levelling when I've got bored of it. I've spent time doing my professions to make money, because I'm prepping to get my mount at lvl 40. I've gone to Darkshore and explored various areas to get a special ghost nightsaber pet. I've grouped and travelled to dungeons like Deadmines and Stockades. All the while making some incredibly memorable runs with good people, with wipes, close calls, and quest lines that have taken an age to finish.

My gear matters too, and if I get something from a dungeon, or a particularly long quest line, it feels momentous; the power increase is tangible. I've even treated myself to an Epic level 37 bow, ready for later on, and it's just sat in my bank waiting. And then, of course, new spells, new talents, I've got my pet to look after; all of it feels that much more potent.
Socially too, I see people about when I'm levelling, high levels, low levels, you name it. And we help each other; we chat about gear, about specs, buff each other as we pass, talk nonsense.

I had a group of four players jump in to save me from dying to a difficult quest mob in Duskwood, for no other reason than to help. They gained nothing from it. That's just one example where I've made new friends in-game.

Because it takes so long to do anything in classic — to travel, to learn — and because the world is so dangerous, because it's not easily accessible (there aren't even any summoning stones in Forever), your decisions and commitments matter.

If I were to re-roll, it would take me another two days, maybe more, to get that character to 30. As a result, I've become attached to the people I've met, my gear, my character as a whole. Even my server. If I see a level 40 to 60, there's a sense of almost awe, like "yeah, one day I'll be that level, that kitted out; I wonder what that'll be like?"

It's aspirational, and the lack of catch-up mechanics contributes to that; it doesn't impede it. It's not that there's no vertical progression here either; there is certainly in Classic, and in fact arguably that's what makes it more interesting, not less.

Get to max level, and you gear up via dungeons. Then you're set for the 10-man raids. After that, you move into Molten Core, Onyxia's Lair, and Blackwing Lair. Finally, you're set for high-end content like Ahn'Qiraj and Naxxramas. It's a long journey upwards.

If you don't have good enough gear on your character, you'll underperform or be unable to compete on the next level of content. But all of that content from day one is still relevant. Catch a glimpse of those players running around the capital cities, and you're struck by it.
It's visually impressive; they've committed that time to the game, that character, that class, and they're powerful as a result. You can see it, certainly with no transmog.
Imperfection makes it more, not less, sociable

By all accounts, Classic World of Warcraft, and subsequently Forever, are flawed games. Certainly, from a shareholder perspective. You have this massive time investment from developers building content that only a select few will see. It takes an age to get to max level compared to modern WoW, and its slower pace can feel like drudgery in direct comparison to the live button-masher mode we have in Midnight.

But it's that lack of accessibility, that need for time, that gives Forever and Classic their sense of sociability. It makes you feel attached to the world, your class, your character, your race; it feels inhabited, and it's that that makes it feel like a true MMO.

World of Warcraft Forever is heavily based on Classic. Blizzard has stated that many, many times over. The entire game is built on or forged from the idea of what Classic might have looked like in an alternate timeline, where the developers added new content but stayed true to the original design principles.
They have arguably deviated in certain examples already, of course. For example, the game already features a number of quality-of-life improvements to classes, a group finder, and cosmetics.

From what I've seen, however, Forever is already on a good path. It'll be less vertical gear treadmill and more slight horizontal incline. From what we've seen so far, general levelling and gearing is almost on par with Classic, albeit mildly quicker.

What Blizzard needs to do, in this humble journo's opinion, is to keep the pace the same. Instead of rushing to deploy new content, or forbidding themselves from adding something on arbitrary, subjective "staying true to the Vanilla World of Warcraft experience" guidelines, they instead need to be asking, "does this reduce the time commitment, or make the game more accessible?"
If either answer is yes, then there's room for discussion.
Can Retail World of Warcraft be saved?

But what of the ailing beast? What of Midnight and its rapid-paced, cartoonish Mythic+ dominated landscape, filled with timers, rewards, and catch-up mechanics galore? What could be pulled from Forever beyond better shaders and volumetric fog? It's a challenging question to answer. Midnight has an active player base, people who love it. Those who live for the high-intensity and flip-flopping nature of chasing the meta. To change that game and make it more Classic, could be intrinsically unpopular.

And yet, we'll have to see exactly how well World of Warcraft: Forever does. If it is what we expect it to be and it dwarfs Midnight's player base by a considerable margin, it's not likely Blizzard will ignore that.

I genuinely believe slower-paced levelling, a lack of catch-up mechanics, and a simplified gearing system would dramatically improve Midnight, and in fact would've improved everything from the Battle of Azeroth expansion onwards. Whether that comes to pass, well, we'll have to wait and see. For now, you can find me buried headfirst in what World of Warcraft should have been, and probably should've stuck to, all those years ago.

articles.headline: Israeli president picks Gadi Eisenkot to form government: Statement
keyFacts: Israeli President Isaac Herzog chose Gadi Eisenkot to have the first opportunity to form a new Israeli government.
The decision follows an October election where neither Eisenkot's alliance nor Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's camp secured a majority.
Eisenkot will attend a formal ceremony on Sunday to begin what will likely be complicated coalition talks.
body: Israeli President Isaac Herzog has chosen Gadi Eisenkot to have the first opportunity to form a new Israeli government, according to a statement released by his office on Saturday evening.

The statement said Eisenkot was informed of Herzog's "intention to task him with forming a government" and would be invited to the president's residence, where a formal ceremony will take place on Sunday.
The decision comes after a neck-and-neck race with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in an election late in October.
Eisenkot's wide-ranging group, fashioned in opposition to Netanyahu, won 48 of the Israeli parliament's 120 seats in October's elections. Netanyahu's camp secured 53, leaving neither with a majority.
Former Israeli military chief Eisenkot is the leader of the centrist Yashar party and heads an anti-Netanyahu alliance.
Neither his nor Netanyahu's blocs secured a majority, with both falling short of the required 61 seats.
While Netanyahu ruled out working with Arab parties to gain a majority, both Arab majority lists had announced during the week that they would recommend Eisenkot to be next prime minister.
What happens next?
The move is the first step toward what will almost certainly be complicated coalition talks.
Should Eisenkot succeed in forming a government, he would take over as prime minister from Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving premier
More to come.

articles.headline: Mass shooting in Polish market leaves at least 6 dead, 15 injured
keyFacts: Six people were killed and 15 others were injured when a gunman opened fire in an open market in Krakow, Poland, authorities said.
Police shot, wounded, and apprehended the lone suspect, who is a Polish citizen, according to officials.
Polish police and government officials stated that the investigation into the background and circumstances of the attack is ongoing.
body: A man drove into an open market in the Polish city of Krakow and opened fire from his car, killing at least six people and injuring at least 15 others, authorities said. The shooter was shot by police and taken into custody.

The shooting happened in the Main Market Square in Krakow around 3 p.m. local time on Saturday. Krakow police said the alleged shooter began firing at random people from his car. Police said the victims were four women and two men.
Marcin Kierwiński, Poland's interior minister, said there were indications the suspect was fascinated by far-right ideology, according to Reuters.

Police officers are among the wounded. The perpetrator was shot and wounded during a confrontation with police a short distance away from the initial violence, and was taken to a hospital for treatment.
The death toll earlier stood at five, but the Malopolski regional government updated it to six in a post on X.
Kierwiński wrote on X that two police officers were wounded by gunfire and one is in serious condition.
"Police officers in Kraków risked their lives to intervene. Immediately. Thanks to their heroic actions, the attacker was quickly apprehended," he wrote.
In a social media post, Krakow police said the gunman is a Polish citizen and that he acted alone.

Katarzyna Cisło, a spokesperson for the Krakow police, told TVN24 that the suspected gunman was wearing military-style fatigues and used a military-type long gun in the attack. Police found many pieces of other weapons, as well as ammunition, in his car.

"I am being kept informed by the Minister of the Interior about the situation in Krakow following the tragic shooting," Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk wrote on social media, adding that "the police are investigating the background and all the circumstances of the attack."
He later headed to Krakow from the capital, Warsaw, a government spokesperson said.
Other details were not immediately available.
Krakow mayor Łukasz Gibała said the city will be in official mourning until Wednesday. He vowed that Krakow will remain open to visitors despite the tragedy.
"The square will belong to us again," Gibała said in a video posted to X.

"We are just learning details of the horrific mass shooting in Krakow, a savage and murderous attack that's shattered the peace of Poland," Tom Rose, the U.S. ambassador to Poland, wrote on X. "America stands with Poland at this dark hour as Poland stands with her beloved citizens of Krakow."
Mass shootings are uncommon in Poland, a European Union and NATO member of 38 million people.

"I saw a man shooting at people and walking around the square," Annette, a woman in her sixties, told news wire Agence France-Presse. "It's a tragedy for Krakow; we've never seen anything like this before."
Kaja Kallas, the European Union's top diplomat, said in a statement that the EU stands with Poland and offered her condolences.

"The tragic loss of life in the shooting in Kraków is a tragedy that will be felt far beyond Poland," she wrote on X. "Poland's strength lies in the resilience of its people. In this moment of grief, Poland does not stand alone."
Krakow is the second-largest city in Poland and roughly 155 miles from the capital, Warsaw.

articles.headline: Trump says he asked Dana White, UFC boss, to be his new White House press secretary
keyFacts: Donald Trump said he offered the position of White House press secretary to UFC chief executive Dana White.
Trump said he also asked White to bring six UFC fighters to serve as White House press aides.
White did not immediately respond to the job offer, according to the article.
body: Donald Trump has offered the job of White House press secretary to Dana White, the chief executive of the Ultimate Fighting Championship, the president said in a social media post on Saturday.

Trump described White, who staged a cage-fighting spectacle at the White House to mark the president’s 80th birthday in June, as “a violent Fighter and Warrior”, credentials unlike any ever used to describe previous press secretaries.

Trump added that he asked White, a vocal supporter who campaigned for him in 2024, to bring six UFC fighters with him to serve as press aides. “We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left,” Trump wrote. “Dana, please take the job!”

It was unclear if the job offer was part of an actual plan, or an attention-grabbing stunt from a president desperate to change the subject from the huge losses suffered by his party in elections this week.
There was no immediate response from White, who, some observer noted, might be loth to leave a lucrative role running the UFC, which has earned him a fortune estimated to be in excess of $600m.

The president’s post was illustrated by seven images, including what appeared to be an AI-generated image of White behind the presidential seal in a press room, and photographs of the six UFC fighters whom Trump fantasizes about deploying to deal with reporters who ask him awkward questions: Islam Makhachev and Khabib Nurmagomedov (who are both from Russia), Justin Gaethje, Daniel Cormier, Amanda Nunes and Kayla Harrison – whose last name was mistakenly rendered as “Harris” by the president.

In his post, Trump acknowledged that two of his dream hires, Makhachev and Nurmagomedov, are not Americans, but he did not mention that Nurmagomedov is reportedly close to the Russian president, Vladimir Putin, or that Makhachev has spoken out in defense of Palestinian civilians killed by Israel in Gaza. In 2023, Makhachev also celebrated a victory in one fight by saying, “Alhamdulillah,” the Arabic phrase for “praise be to God” used by Muslims. Democrat Abdul El-Sayed was criticized in the rightwing media for using that same Arabic phrase in his victory speech this week.

The first in a series of taxpayer-funded pro-Trump ads broadcast by the White House in the run-up to the recent midterms closed with images of the UFC fight on Trump’s birthday and remarks about him from White, who could be heard saying: “He is the toughest, most resilient human being I have ever met in my life.” White used that formulation to describe Trump multiple times during the 2024 presidential election campaign, most notably to sing Trump’s praises at the Republican national convention.

articles.headline: Letitia James brags that she’ll continue to ‘sue, baby, sue’ in latest threat directed at Trump
keyFacts: New York Attorney General Letitia James told supporters at a conference she will continue using the law to sue high-cost oligarchs.
The article noted that James has sued Donald Trump, his administration, and his businesses more than 70 times since 2019.
Governor Kathy Hochul committed to implementing a statewide universal 4-K program in New York by 2028.
body: Embattled New York Attorney General Letitia James aimed a fresh threat at President Trump this week — bragging that she’ll continue to “sue, baby, sue” while claiming she’s targeting “oligarchs.”

The far-left state prosecutor – emboldened after being re-elected to another four years in office on Tuesday — did not mention the president by name, yet all but gloated that she will continue to target him while addressing supporters on Friday at the SOMOS political conference in Puerto Rico.
“Mortgages are too high, interest rates are too high, car insurance is too high,” said James to applause.
“We’ve got to make sure all of the oligarchs that are at the top are imposing all of these high costs on New Yorkers and Americans.
“I’m excited to get back to work and to use the law — both as a sword and as a shield — and sue baby sue with all of you! God bless you and thank you.”

James – who has long been accused of pursuing partisan political witch hunts against the president and his allies, even after failing to dig up dirt – has reportedly sued Trump, his administration and his businesses well over 70 times since taking office in 2019.
She did win a massive $454 million civil judgment against Trump’s business for allegedly inflating its value, but a state appeals court overturned the decision last year.

On Saturday at the conference, Gov. Kathy Hochul touted her pledge to expand universal childcare statewide by 2028 while speaking at the annual SOMOS Labor Breakfast on Saturday — as she faces rising pressure from NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani and his lefty allies to hike levies in the wake of Democrats’ midterm domination.

“I’ve already invested $12 billion in child care — $4.5 billion this year alone — but I have made a commitment. I want a fully universal 4-K program across the state of New York by 2028,” said Hochul.
During her remarks, the governor also badly botched an attempted joke about encouraging a young family to stay in New York, instead of moving to Philadelphia.
“I said, why do you want to go to Philadelphia? You like the Knicks better or something?” she said, before realizing she had thrown up an airball of a joke.

“I don’t understand. You don’t like the Knicks? You like [Philadelphia 76ers star] Lebron James? I don’t understand. I don’t understand. Thank you. The Knicks are here. But he said he wanted to, but they couldn’t afford the rent and childcare on top of it.”
Both Hochul and Mamdani – who was also at the breakfast – refused to speak to media members afterwards.

articles.headline: "This trailer is my way of saying goodbye": Have a listen to the Mass Effect 5 score that could have been, courtesy of one of the original games' composers
keyFacts: Original trilogy composer Sam Hulick shared a re-scored version of the leaked Mass Effect Universe trailer for N7 Day as a personal farewell.
Hulick stated that BioWare had previously contacted him to potentially contribute music to an internal demo for the project.
EA is shutting down BioWare and Mass Effect 5 has been cancelled.
body: By this point I'm probably safe in assuming that you all know EA are shutting down BioWare, and that Mass Effect 5 has been cancelled in turn. You may have also seen that an internal trailer for Mass Effect 5, or Universe as it was seemingly going to be called, was leaked not long after the news broke, and that Sam Hulick, one of the composers on the original trilogy of games, shared he was going to offer up his re-scored version of the trailer. Well, it's N7 Day, as rough as that will be for many of the developers on the game, but Hulick has stood by his word, and shared an oral glimpse at what the world of Mass Effect Universe could have sounded like.

You can check out this new version of the trailer below, perhaps pop it on while you have a read of the rest of this post, as Hulick did also write in a Patreon blog about his experience with the series. "As part of my own closure, and as a love letter to the fans, I really wanted to re-score the leaked Mass Effect Universe trailer in time for N7 Day this year," he wrote. "BioWare edited a killer track called “Quartz” by French 79 to fit their trailer, which I think hinted at a slight directional shift in the score. Using that as inspiration, along with the musical tone from my work on the first three Mass Effect games, I hit the studio and got to work."

As it turns out, BioWare had actually reached out to Hulick asking him to potentially do some work for the project. "This year, BioWare emailed me asking if I was interested in working with them on an internal demo, and they said they were 'hoping to get some music written that would feel like Mass [Effect], supporting our new direction.' Of course, I said yes!" This doesn't mean he wouldn't have composed the actual game, as a composer hadn't been officially selected, but Hulick said he was "more than happy to collaborate on the new game’s musical direction and help make their internal demo sound as good as it could."

Hulick also spoke of some of the ideas he had for the direction Mass Effect Universe's soundtrack could take, noting how he "thought it would’ve been incredible to bring more songs with lyrics into the game," considering how many people loved the first game's end-credits song. "This would’ve been a great way to highlight more emotional moments in the narrative. Artists at the top of my collaboration list included Gunship, NINA, and The Midnight, all of whom have a moody, cinematic synthwave vibe that would’ve meshed well with the score in my head. And I’m pretty sure the Gunship guys are gamers, and if they’re Mass Effect fans, that would’ve been the icing on the cake!"

Of course, with the studio now closing, this never got to go very far, the news hitting Hulick "particularly hard, as the Mass Effect trilogy is a core part of my origin story as a composer." For the composer, ultimately "this trailer is my way of saying goodbye… at least for now." This continues to be a horrendously sad moment in the industry! As always, solidarity with the team at BioWare.

articles.headline: Former Rockstar Developer Says They Should Hurry Up On GTA 6’s PC Version Before AI Gets There First
keyFacts: Former Rockstar developer Obbe Vermeij said the studio should prioritize releasing GTA 6 on PC before AI technology enables unofficial ports.
Vermeij stated that AI models can now decompile games and convert console versions, potentially hurting sales for publishers like Take-Two.
Rockstar traditionally builds games for console specifications first, a strategy Vermeij believes AI developments could soon force them to change.
body: Grand Theft Auto, a gravity well in the gaming universe, is the most anticipated release this generation. Mere weeks away, it has reshaped the world around it, all despite being a console-first, single player experience. Speaking with Rock Paper Shotgun, former Rockstar developer Obbe Vermeij commented on the companyâs unique release priorities when it comes to PC versions, but speculates that could change with AI copycats breathing down its neck.

“I would be concerned if I was Rockstar,” says Vermeij, “somebody would just take the PS5 version and get AI to change it to PC, which won’t be as good as their effort, but it could still also hurt their sales.”

While he hasnât worked at the studio since 2009, Vermeij acted as technical director on Grand Theft Auto III. He said when the company ported the first game to the PlayStation in 1997, there were frustrations with how much had to be compromised from the PC build. Heading into the PlayStation 2, they opted to build for console specs first instead of being forced to pare down. Somewhat unconventional for a game that initially made its home on computers, but it proved to be the correct approach, giving the series a massive player base and launching it into global infamy.

AI could change this philosophy, according to Vermeij. While AI struggles to make original games, film, any art as well as the living, human counterparts it pilfers from, it has proven to be prolific at decompiling games. Able to disassemble and reassemble the parts of a game, it has accelerated mods and ports for existing games in recent months. The latest models of popular AI clients have proven to be a Pandoraâs Box. Its flooded Steam with vibe codedâ shovelware, frustrated vulnerable indie developers, disenfranchised existing modding communities, but also become a thorn in the side of major publishers, whose catalogues are just as susceptible to this form of tinkering.

“A big company like Take-Two, they would be able to get the lawyers on the case,” says Vermeij. “It’s a brave new world. What was the case before, is that there’s so much effort in developing the game, that it is not possible to rip it off, and that’s completely changed now.”

While pre-LLM machine learning-assisted ports were already a sore spot for Grand Theft Auto, Vermeij doesnât think an unofficial, AI-made PC port of the upcoming VI would meet the standards Rockstar boasts. Vermeij isnât an AI hold-out either, using the tech for his own current projects, like the environmental sim Plentiful. Regardless, the prospect of overnight ersatz threatens to prick at Rockstarâs internal release schedule, having already been deflated by high-profile leaks.

articles.headline: CENTCOM announces task force to blockade Iranian ground transit routes
keyFacts: U.S. Central Command announced Task Force Iron Gate to blockade Iranian ground transit routes and prevent illegal shipments.
Adm. Brad Cooper said the new task force will constrain Iran's ability to finance terrorism and replenish its military.
Former official Joe Kent criticized the announcement as provocation that could escalate tensions and undermine ongoing peace talks.
body: U.S. Central Command announced on Saturday a new task force designed to blockade Iranian ground transit routes used to transport illegal shipments.

Task Force Iron Gate will work with U.S. agencies to help prevent the movement of advanced weapons, dual-use technologies, sanctioned materials, and illegal revenue streams across Iran’s borders and the Caspian Sea amid war.

The move shows that the commander of CENTCOM is committed to finding alternative methods of disrupting Iranian forces as President Donald Trump considers further military action against the Islamic regime.

“The establishment of Task Force Iron Gate reinforces the success of our ironclad blockade against Iran at sea,” Adm. Brad Cooper said in a statement . “Strengthening CENTCOM’s collaboration with U.S. interagency partners will further constrain Iran’s ability to finance terrorism, rebuild weapons factories, and replenish their military.”
The U.S. military’s naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz “has prevented Iran from exporting more than $25 billion in crude oil,” CENTCOM noted. The naval blockade remains in place.

While diplomatic efforts between the United States and Iran are actively underway, Trump confirmed on Friday that there were limited, “minor” strikes against an Iranian air defense system on Qeshm Island. The island is located in Iran’s crucial waterway for oil shipments. The president has not yet given the order for more aggressive attacks on Iran.

Over two hours after CENTCOM revealed its new task force, former National Counterterrorism Center Director Joe Kent publicly disagreed with the action, saying it will only escalate tensions with Iran further and undermine peace talks.

“The Iranians have made it clear that they won’t accept negotiations while under threat of escalation,” he posted on X . “Iranian leadership has stated there will either be war or there will be peace, but they will not sit idly by and wait for the next attack & they won’t tolerate being slowly strangled by sanctions.”

Kent resigned from his administration position in March, weeks after the U.S. and Israeli militaries first bombed Iran. He argued that “Iran posed no imminent threat to our nation” and that the conflict started due to pressure from Israel and its American lobby.
Nearly eight months after his resignation, Kent called CENTCOM’s announcement about additional sanctions on Iran “brash provocation.”

The former counterterrorism official pointed to the midterm election results as evidence that the “American people do not support this war.” Notably, he said Trump’s decision to appoint Stephen Miller as the new White House chief of staff may have been made to help end the war.
Vice President JD Vance has been engaging in indirect talks over the past two weeks to end the conflict, Axios reported on Friday. Trump confirmed talks concerning Iran were taking place.
Kent claimed CENTCOM is “working directly against what President Trump is attempting to accomplish” in the Middle East , which is why he believes Trump needs new advisers.

“It’s become abundantly clear that the President needs to install a new national security team, one that’s not tied to starting the war and that can instead end it,” Kent said. “To do that, he needs people who can & will get the national security state under control, not submit to it.”
MASSIE GIVES HEGSETH IMPEACHMENT ULTIMATUM AS GOP PINS BLUE WAVE ON IRAN WAR
Secretary of State Marco Rubio serves as the permanent national security adviser, working with War Secretary Pete Hegseth and Miller, among other officials.

Trump has said he plans to fire some Cabinet members without disclosing them. Hegseth is in a highly vulnerable position the longer the Iran war lasts. When the House returns on Monday, the voting process for Hegseth’s articles of impeachment is expected to commence.

articles.headline: Dropout’s Vic Michaelis Wants to Toss Their Star Wars Character Out a Window
keyFacts: Dropout star Vic Michaelis voiced the character Runa Blask in the video game Star Wars Zero Company.
Michaelis said their improv comedy background helped prepare them for their first-ever video game role.
Fans have embraced Runa for her constant jokes, though the character does not go on combat missions and cannot be harmed.
body: Dropout star Vic Michaelis used to fall asleep to Attack of the Clones. Not because they hated it, like so many Star Wars prequel detractors, but because it was their comfort watch. “I've seen the first 45 minutes of Episode II, I want to say, 300 times,” Michaelis told Polygon. “It's so comforting. The prequels hold a place in my heart where it is like nothing bad can happen when I'm watching them.”

Michaelis has now gone from watching Star Wars to being a part of the larger Star Wars universe. In Star Wars Zero Company, they played breakout character Runa Blask, the wise-cracking advisor to the titular mercenary group, led by Captain Hawks.

Michaelis hails from the improv comedy world, but they’ve done film and scripted TV shows as well. Zero Company was their first-ever video game role. “I was so simultaneously terrified, obviously, of the video game aspect of it and also, you know, the Star Wars of it all.”
Turns out, that fear was unnecessary. The team at Bit Reactor was familiar with Michaelis’ Dropout work, and that was part of the reason they wanted Michaelis for the role.

Their improv background helped influence their performance, though they weren’t changing lines or jokes. “The improv is so much about the preparation in a way that I think people don't really know.” Instead, all of Runa’s best quips were already in the very strong script. “All of my favorite lines that Runa had were written or pitched lines from the writers,” Michaelis said.

Among those lines were many instances of Runa saying “wizard,” which basically means “cool” in Star Wars. “Runa's very tall, everything is ‘wizard,’” Michaelis said with a laugh, joking they must have said the word “500 times.”

Fans have glommed onto Runa for her constant jokes and ribbing of Hawks. “I'm seeing a lot of people being like, ‘Runa, I love her, and I wanna throw her out a window.’ Which I really resonate with, and I think was part of what we were going for,” Michaelis said. “Big sister vibes.”

Runa can’t be thrown out a window. She actually can’t be harmed at all. While the game features a permadeath feature for its operators, Runa doesn’t go on combat missions and doesn’t leave The Den, Zero Company’s headquarters.

“I did start seeing people devastated and heartbroken that some characters that they put a lot of time and energy into didn't make it through,” Michaelis said. “Do I wish people sort of mourned me in that way? Maybe. I don't know. I’m going to be thinking about that.”

Before Runa was a member of Zero Company, she was a self-described “freelance consultant to the top corporations and families in the galaxy.” AKA, a Separatist financial fixer. She desires a fortune that working for Zero Company will never grant her. As she tells Hawks, if she had that fortune, she’d want to buy a moon and run a resort. Michaelis has much humbler aspirations if they were to live in the world of Star Wars. “I would want to be a small business owner,” Michaelis said, and started describing what would make for a very fun Disney Plus show.

“I want to do a comedy night at my bookstore and all of a sudden, you've got a bunch of interplanetary politics or some red tape of why I can't do this. Then I'm marching up to the Republic with my civil city ordinances, trying to get this comedy night happening, and I'm accidentally now involved and implicated in a sort of a greater plot,” Michaelis said. “And all I wanted to do was try and get a couple of standups at my bookstore at night so I could sell wine after hours.”
If Star Trek can have a critically acclaimed animated sitcom, why can’t Star Wars have a series about a store owner just trying to get a comedy night off the ground? Your move, Disney.

articles.headline: Parents want safer phones for kids. These companies are answering the call.
keyFacts: Companies are developing kid-friendly phones with restricted software and companion apps to address parents' concerns about unrestricted smartphone access.
Popular options like The Bark Phone, Gabb, Pinwheel, and Teracube offer modified mobile devices with parental controls and varying levels of content monitoring.
Other companies provide minimalist mobile devices, home phones, or landlines such as Ooma MyPhone, Tin Can, Waffle, and Yello! for restricted communication.
body: As parents become increasingly concerned about the potential dangers of unrestricted smartphone access for children, a growing number of companies are developing devices specifically designed for kids.

Today’s kid-friendly phones typically feature touchscreens, cameras, and communication capabilities similar to regular smartphones. However, the software on these devices is heavily modified to remove or restrict access to web browsers, social media, app stores, and other distractions.

Parents can usually manage these devices through a companion app, allowing them to approve contacts, monitor locations, set screen time limits, select available apps, and, in some cases, receive alerts regarding cyberbullying, explicit content, or online predators.
In addition to these modified devices, some companies offer a more minimalist approach, creating devices that focus solely on calling and texting.
There are also home phones designed specifically for children, like Tin Can and the recently launched Pinwheel Home.
Here’s a look at the major players shaping the kid-phone market.
The Bark Phone
The Bark Phone is probably one of the most popular kid-specific smartphones on the market.

Built on Samsung Galaxy hardware and powered by Bark’s monitoring software, it only allows calls and texts with approved contacts. Bark continuously scans texts, emails, photos, and supported apps for signs of cyberbullying, grooming, suicidal ideation, sexual content, and other potential concerns, then sends alerts to parents.
A big standout feature is that parents can gradually unlock web browsing, apps, and other features as their child matures. The phone also includes GPS tracking and screen-time management.
Current pricing for the standard model is $240, plus a required wireless plan beginning at $29/month. Higher-tier plans add internet access and unlimited texting.
Gabb
Gabb is a well-known name in the kid-friendly phone category. Unlike Bark, however, Gabb focuses less on monitoring content and more on eliminating online risks altogether.

Its phones don’t include social media, a browser, or an app store. Instead, children get calling, texting, and a carefully curated selection of preloaded apps, including a camera, calendar, and calculator. The company also touts its “worry-free” music streaming library with millions of songs.
Additionally, parents can view location and manage certain device settings, while optional services such as “Gabb Guard” help block spam calls and unwanted texts.
Current phone pricing starts around $159.99, with cellular service starting around $24.99 per month.
Pinwheel
With Pinwheel, parents approve every app, control contacts, schedule screen time, create custom routines, and monitor location history.

One standout feature is the ability to create different “modes” throughout the day. For example, limiting the phone to calling and navigation during school hours before unlocking additional features after homework.

Pinwheel phones start around $119, while the Caregiver Portal subscription begins at $14.99 per month without cell service. (Cellular service can be purchased separately through participating carriers.)
The company recently launched two landline phones for $68 and $79. It also offers a smartwatch at $160.
Teracube Thrive

Launched in 2022, Teracube offers a tailored version of Android known as Thrive OS. This enables parents to approve every app download, filter web browsing, set app-specific and overall screen-time limits, monitor location, and create customized routines for school or bedtime. However, because it has more traditional smartphone features, it’s often recommended for older children.
Thrive currently sells for $99, with plans starting at $35 per month.
Ooma MyPhone
Unlike the other products in this roundup, Ooma MyPhone isn’t a mobile phone at all. This kid-focused home phone is designed as a modern replacement for the traditional household landline.

The service allows calls only between approved contacts through its Trusted Circle feature, offers scheduled Quiet Hours, provides address-based 911 service, sends emergency alerts when 911 is dialed, and lets parents review call logs through an online portal. There are no apps, internet browsing, texting, or social media.
The phone costs $99.99, while service starts at $7.99 per month.
Tin Can
For $100, Tin Can resembles a landline phone with a distinctive tin can design, which is the inspiration behind its name.

This device does not require a traditional phone jack, but connects via Wi-Fi. Only approved contacts can make calls, effectively preventing spam or unauthorized communications. Parents can easily manage contacts through a user-friendly companion app.
Tin Can offers a free plan for calling other Tin Can users, as well as a $9.99 per month plan that allows calls to all approved contacts.
Waffle

A newer entrant in the space, Waffle recently opened preorders for its screen-free devices: Waffle Home ($119), a landline phone, and Waffle Go ($169), which looks like a portable walkie-talkie or kids’ toy with three simple buttons that can only make voice calls and listen to voice notes.
Parents can approve contacts via the companion app, as well as see location and control when devices can call.
The new phones will ship on November 23.
Yello!

TextNow, the Canadian telecommunications company, recently launched its new mobile phone for kids. It’s called Yello! and while it looks like a normal touchscreen smartphone, it doesn’t have an app store, social media, or unrestricted web access.
Parents can see their kids’ location and battery life, as well as control things like the games they play and who they have in their contacts.
Yello! costs $149.99 upfront, with a $19.99 per month plan.
